# Historical ATML oracle

`legacy-atml.json` contains outputs generated by the original Python
`HtmlAtmlGenerator._render_node`, not by the TypeScript implementation. Its
metadata records the original file's SHA-256. Each case names its historical
source test. The HTML is serialized from those tests' literal extracted trees;
tooltip and listener metadata become equivalent HTML attributes.

Regenerate from the original Python renderer file with Python 3 (standard library),
Node and the installed Playwright Chromium browser:

```powershell
python tests/fixtures/generate-legacy-atml.py <renderer.py> <unit-tests-directory>
```

The script excludes application imports and async entry points using Python's
AST. Original renderer methods and constants execute unchanged with each case's
configuration. `tree` records original mock input; `renderTree` adapts it to the
TypeScript tree shape using the Python flatten/class/attribute decisions.
`expected` is the original renderer output. `legacy.render.spec.ts` compares
content and nonempty line boundaries after removing leading ASCII spaces,
blank lines and CLI-only `: ` text markers, and normalizing `id=value` to `#id`.
The CLI starts at column zero, indents text and omits historical separators.
`render.spec.ts` separately checks
exact indentation, meaningful text spaces, the absence of blank separators and
depth limits.
No copied or rewritten renderer serves as the oracle.

For `browserExpected`, the original `_extract_dom_tree` JavaScript string runs
unchanged inside Chromium on the serialized HTML, then Python renders the
result. This is deliberately distinct from mock-tree output: a span containing
only whitespace is trimmed by real DOM extraction, while the old mock test
passed that whitespace directly to the renderer.

`legacy.browser.spec.ts` exercises fixture HTML through the actual CLI and
compares to `browserExpected`, stripping `: ` text markers, added numeric `:` refs
and leading ASCII spaces, and omitting blank separator lines. Leading `:id`
references and `id=value` attributes are converted back to `#id`. It retains unquoted
text, trailing spaces, original IDs and attribute order. Add the suite to Chromium and Firefox
`testMatch` if the project selection changes.

This oracle covers the historical renderer's input domain. Live form state,
password suppression, frame/shadow traversal and CLI reference lifetime have
separate tests in `browser.spec.ts`; they extend the old extractor and are not
claimed as historical extraction parity. The old `html_visible` browser scripts
asserting literal HTML tags are not valid ATML oracles.
